text.p: American Express Co said Thursday it was realigning some of its business units including American Express Financial Direct, which will become part of American Exprress Financial Advisors.
Also, American Express Tax & Business Services (TBS) will become a part of the American Express Small Business Services.
The company said Bill Heron has decided to resign as president of American Express Financial Direct but will stay on until a successor is named and to help with the transition.

"Overall, the changes are designed to place businesses that serve similar markets under common management and enable us to serve customer more effectively," chairman and chief executive Harvey Golub and president Ken Chenault said in a letter to employees.
The TBS unit had been part of Workplace Financial Services. Workplace will be disbanded and its units will be shifted elsewhere.
Financial Direct, which includes an online brokerage service, was established as a stand-alone business in May, 1996.
Referring to Financial Direct, Golub and Chenault said in the memo that there is a "need to expand our product offerings and attract new customers to the franchise more quickly than we have."
The memo said American Express is committed to expanding its advisor, direct and third-party distribution channels.
